info.name: Init Server API
info.description:
Business Associate, Vendor & Admin Management Service APIs

Seeded Users (npm run db:reset creates these):
- Admin: admin@test.com
- Vendor: vendor@test.com
- BA: ba@test.com
- Customer: customer@test.com

Password for all four: Qa-Test-99  (override with SEED_ADMIN_PASSWORD)

Note: Auth uses httpOnly cookies. Enable 'Send cookies' in Postman settings.

AUTH REWRITE (2026-08-24): sessions moved to Redis, one per DEVICE. Cookies issued before this change are invalid - log in again. New: GET/DELETE /sessions per portal, POST /oauth/:provider, and RateLimit-* headers on every response. Redis 7+ and a running Redis are required or the server refuses to boot.

PASSWORD POLICY: registration requires 8+ characters and rejects breached passwords (HIBP), so a short common password like "Test1234" is refused even though it is long enough.

CSRF: login/register/oauth responses include data.csrfToken; their test scripts save it to {{csrfToken}}. Logout, logout-all, switch-role, request-role and DELETE /sessions send it as the x-csrf-token header. Without it they return 403.

item.name: Auth Scenarios
item.description: End-to-end auth behaviour, not endpoint coverage - the portal folders above already cover each route once. Run the numbered requests in order within each subfolder; they depend on the state the previous one leaves behind.

item.name: 3. Revoke one device
item.description: Log in from a second Postman environment first so there is another device to kill. Uses {{otherSid}}, saved by request 2.

item.name: 4. Revoke someone else's session - expect 404
item.description: Ownership check. A guessed sid must not be revocable.

item.name: 5. Google login
item.description: Set {{googleIdToken}} to a real Google ID token, and GOOGLE_CLIENT_IDS in .env to the client id that minted it. Without those this returns 401 - which is itself a valid test that verification is enforced.

exec: pm.test('200 with a valid token, 401 with an invalid one', () => {

item.name: 7. Rate limit - run 11+ times to trip it
item.description: Login is limited by IP AND account: 10 per 15 minutes by default (RATE_LIMIT_LOGIN_MAX). Use Postman's Collection Runner with 12 iterations. Watch RateLimit-Remaining count down, then a 429 with Retry-After.

exec: pm.test('401 for a wrong password', () => pm.response.to.have.status(401));
pm.test('session is dead after logout-all', () => pm.response.to.have.status(401));

item.name: 10. Admin - list devices
item.description: Same two endpoints exist on every portal. Log in at /admin/auth/login first; the admin cookie is separate from the customer one.

item.name: 11. Weak password rejected
item.description: Policy is 12+ characters, no composition rules. Enforced in password.service, not in the schema - one source of truth.

item.name: 12. Breached password rejected
item.description: HIBP k-anonymity check: only the first 5 SHA-1 chars leave the server. Fails OPEN, so a 201 here means HIBP was unreachable - not that the check is broken.

exec: pm.test('400 when HIBP knows it, 201 if HIBP unreachable (fails open)', () => {

item.name: 13. Invalid email rejected
item.description: zod at the edge. Before this, garbage fell through to the generic auth failure.

item.name: 14. OTP as a JSON number is accepted
item.description: Regression test. A numeric otp used to be compared against a stored string, always failing - and burning one of five attempts on a CORRECT code.

exec: pm.test('not a validation error - the number is coerced', () => {

item.name: 15. Logout without CSRF header - expect 403
item.description: Log in first. This request deliberately sends NO x-csrf-token, so it must be refused. Run request 1 again afterwards to restore a usable session.

item.name: 16. Lockout - run 4 times
item.description: LOCKOUT_MAX_ATTEMPTS=3 in the QA env. Note the response stays a GENERIC 401 even once locked - telling the caller 'account locked' would confirm the address exists. The real reason is in the audit log.

exec: pm.test('401 while under the cap, 401 generic once locked', () => {

item.name: 1. Forgot password - always 200
item.description: Returns the same body for a registered and an unregistered address. An OTP is stored either way - skipping the store for unknown addresses would make remainingAttempts null vs a number, which is an existence oracle by itself.

exec: pm.test('200 regardless of whether the address exists', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));
pm.test('neutral message - no existence leak', () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.match(/if that address/i));

item.name: 2. Forgot password - unknown address, identical response
item.description: Compare this response to request 1 byte for byte. Any difference is an enumeration hole.

exec: pm.test('200, same as a real address', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.name: 3. Verify reset OTP - sets the reset cookie
item.description: Set {{otp}} first. The reset id is 32 CSPRNG bytes - it was Math.random() until 2026-09-01, which was guessable.

exec: pm.test('200 with the correct code', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.name: 4. Reset password - weak one rejected
item.description: The policy applies on reset, not only on register.

item.name: 5. Reset password - succeeds, kills every session
item.description: Also clears the account lockout - reset is the only recovery path a locked-out user has - and revokes every session. Verify by calling GET /sessions with an old cookie: it must 401.

item.name: 6. Reset session is single use
item.description: Run straight after 5. The reset session is deleted on use; replaying it must fail.

exec: pm.test('401 - the session was consumed by request 5', () => pm.response.to.have.status(401));

item.name: 7. Send email verification code
item.description: Same enumeration-proof shape as forgot-password. Only actually emails when the account exists and is unverified.

exec: pm.test('does not reveal whether verification is needed', () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.match(/if that address/i));

item.name: 8. Verify email
item.description: Sets emailVerified and clears the OTP keys. Set {{otp}} from the code sent by request 7.

exec: pm.test('200 on the correct code', () => pm.response.to.have.status(200));

item.name: 9. Wrong OTP burns an attempt
item.description: Five wrong attempts per account per window, then 429. Run 6 times to see the switch.

item.name: 10. Admin reset flow reaches the same handler
item.description: Spot check that a second portal routes into the same shared controller. Admin has no /register or /verify-email by design.

item.name: Session Cache Lifecycle
item.description: The session caches display fields, so every write that changes one must rewrite it (syncSessionUser) or destroy the session (revokeUserSessions). Run in order.

exec: pm.test('served from the session, not the database', () => pm.expect(u.email).to.eql('customer@test.com'));
// The whole point of syncSessionUser: no re-login needed.
pm.test('set customerId before running step 6', () => pm.expect(true).to.be.true);
// Security-critical: authenticate no longer checks user.status, so revocation
// on suspend is the only thing ending a suspended account's access.
pm.test('401 - every session revoked on suspend', () => pm.response.to.have.status(401));
